newsitem.title: UK: NWE GAS OIL SPREADS MIXED AS OUTRIGHT PRICE EASES.
newsitem.headline: NWE GAS OIL SPREADS MIXED AS OUTRIGHT PRICE EASES.

text.p: European gas oil differentials were mixed on Monday but early business was inactive despite signs of better barge buying interest, traders said.
Outright prices eased up to $1 a tonne. The August front month on the IPE slipped around 75 cents to trade at $168.75 a tonne. September eased $1 to trade at $170.000 a tonne.
On the key ARA barge market, 0.2 per cent sulphur heating oil was slightly firmer, reflecting steady losses on the screen.
But traders gave a wide variety of quotes in the absence of a confirmed trade. Prompt Rotterdam refinery heating oil was heard offered at around August IPE +$1.00 to $1.25 fob ARA.
Bid were around 50 cents, some 25 to 50 cents stronger.
Second half August heating oil was heard at around September IPE flat offered. Low sulphur diesel was notionally assessed at August IPE +4.50/$5.50, slightly firmer.
On cargoes, German heating oil was assessed at September IPE +$0.75/$1.50 cif NWE for the second half of August.

Low sulphur diesel for mid-month was notionally the equivalent of August IPE $4.75/$5.75 cif NWE, traders said. In late Friday trade a last decade August 40,000 tonner of Italian heating oil moved at about high fob Med quotes +$2.50.
